summary: Regime read: Tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 76% points tightening, 24% mixed, and 0% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (per U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index). Fed communications are strongly tightening (per Rio Times: Fed Holds US Rate as S&P 500 Gains 0.3%). Employment is strongly tightening and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction, one vote per event cluster (no magnitude averaging)
scoring.clustering: one vote per event_key; representative = max-weight source; keyless sources are singleton clusters

sources.title: Why a CPI surprise could trip up the Fed's rate-cutting plans
sources.evidence_text: The article says an upside CPI surprise could push the Fed toward a pause in rate cuts and keep the policy rate unchanged at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation surprises higher, the Fed is more likely to delay easing to preserve credibility on price stability.

sources.title: Inflation edges up, highlighting Fed's bumpy path to stable prices
sources.evidence_text: The article says October CPI rose to 2.6% year over year, which it described as a bump that still likely would not change the Fed's near-term course.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer inflation print reduces the Fed's room to cut aggressively even if it does not fully reverse the easing cycle.

sources.title: Lower-Than-Expected Inflation Keeps Fed On Track For October Rate Cut
sources.evidence_text: The article says September CPI rose 3.0% year over year, below the expected 3.1%, and argues that this left the Fed on track for cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A downside inflation surprise reduces the immediate need for restraint and supports further easing if labor-market conditions also soften.

sources.title: Tame US inflation gives the Fed room for more rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: ING argued that softer November inflation gave the Fed more room to deliver additional cuts in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A clear disinflation surprise eases the constraint on the Fed's inflation mandate and supports more accommodation.

sources.title: CPI Surprises to the Downside
sources.evidence_text: The article says the latest CPI report came in well below expectations, which improved the odds of Fed rate cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer inflation surprise reduces pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive and supports additional easing.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Rates
sources.evidence_text: The Treasury's October 28 yield-curve data show the 2-year yield at approximately 4.67%.
sources.why_it_matters: An elevated 2-year yield reflects restrictive expected short-term policy and is inconsistent with strong market conviction in imminent rate cuts.

sources.title: Economic News Releases
sources.evidence_text: BLS reported that median weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers were $1,232 in the third quarter of 2026, while its indicator summary listed September average hourly earnings up by $0.05.
sources.why_it_matters: Continued wage growth can sustain services inflation, but the available figures do not establish a decisive acceleration or deceleration in the Fed’s inflation reaction function.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims hover near 57-year lows
sources.evidence_text: Initial unemployment claims fell by 1,000 to 194,000 in the week ended October 24, while claims remained near multi-decade lows.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistently low layoffs indicate labor-market resilience, reducing the urgency for additional Federal Reserve cuts.

sources.title: US unemployment claims slide to 194,000, the lowest since mid-July
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims declined to 194,000, the four-week average fell to 196,750, and continuing claims decreased by 21,000 to about 1.7 million.
sources.why_it_matters: Broadly stable or improving claims data argues against labor-market deterioration that would prompt faster easing.

sources.title: FOMC October 29, 2026 Preview: Gold, Rate Odds & Key Data
sources.evidence_text: The reported December meeting pricing implied a substantially higher probability of a rate increase than a rate cut.
sources.why_it_matters: Market expectations for a hike rather than a cut signal that investors see the policy path drifting toward restraint.

sources.title: Fed Holds US Rate as S&P 500 Gains 0.3%
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve reportedly held the target range at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with two officials favoring a rate increase and inflation described as elevated.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold accompanied by dissenting votes for a hike and concern about elevated inflation indicates limited scope for near-term cuts.

sources.title: FOMC Statement
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve released an FOMC statement on October 28, 2026, but the available search result does not provide its policy decision or detailed wording.
sources.why_it_matters: The policy statement is the primary signal for whether labor-market risks and inflation conditions are shifting the reaction function toward additional easing or restraint.

sources.title: Quarterly Data Series on Business Employment Dynamics
sources.evidence_text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics listed the quarterly Business Employment Dynamics release among its October 28, 2026 releases, but the available result does not show the underlying employment changes.
sources.why_it_matters: Business births, deaths, and employment flows can alter the assessment of labor-market momentum, but the available evidence does not establish a clear easing or tightening signal.

sources.title: Metropolitan Area Employment and Unemployment
sources.evidence_text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics listed the September 2026 metropolitan employment and unemployment release on October 28, 2026, without details in the available result about the national labor-market signal.
sources.why_it_matters: Regional employment and unemployment data inform the Fed’s labor-market assessment, but no directional policy implication can be established from the available summary.

sources.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index
sources.evidence_text: The September PCE price index increased 3.6 percent over the year, remaining well above the Federal Reserve’s 2 percent target.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent above-target PCE inflation argues against further easing and keeps the reaction function focused on restraining price pressures.

sources.title: CPI Home: Consumer Price Index
sources.evidence_text: September CPI rose 0.6 percent month over month and 3.7 percent over the year.
sources.why_it_matters: Elevated headline CPI momentum and annual inflation reduce the case for additional rate cuts.

sources.title: FOMC Statement: October 28, 2026
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve published an October 28 FOMC statement, indicating that price stability remained a central monetary-policy objective.
sources.why_it_matters: Continued emphasis on price stability signals limited tolerance for above-target inflation and constrains an easing interpretation.

sources.title: Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The September PCE price index rose 0.5% monthly and 3.6% from a year earlier.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation materially above the Federal Reserve’s 2% objective argues for fewer near-term cuts and preserves a tightening bias.

sources.title: GDP, 3rd Quarter 2026 — Advance Estimate
sources.evidence_text: The GDP release reported quarterly PCE inflation of 2.1% and core PCE inflation of 2.5%.
sources.why_it_matters: Core inflation remains above target, supporting a cautious reaction function even though the quarterly readings are less acute than headline September PCE.

sources.title: U.S. Economy at a Glance
sources.evidence_text: The employment cost index increased 0.9% in the second quarter of 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Quarterly compensation growth is steady rather than accelerating, providing limited evidence either for additional easing or renewed tightening.

sources.title: Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged despite elevated inflation
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve held its target rate at 3.75%–4.00% while describing inflation as elevated after raising rates by 25 basis points at the prior meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A pause after a recent hike, combined with elevated inflation, indicates the reaction function is prioritizing disinflation over additional easing.

sources.title: Fed meeting live updates: Interest rates held steady in split vote
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC voted 10–2 to hold rates, with two officials dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point hike, while futures implied a higher probability of a December increase.
sources.why_it_matters: Hawkish dissents and increased near-term hike risk show policy risks have shifted away from cuts and toward further tightening.

sources.title: Fed rate decision October 2026
sources.evidence_text: September consumer-price inflation was reported at 3.7% year over year, while core inflation was expected to rise to 3.1%.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation materially above the 2% target reduces room for rate cuts and raises the likelihood that restrictive policy must persist.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady as it awaits more information
sources.evidence_text: The Fed held rates steady, upgraded its assessment of economic growth to a strong pace, and said inflation remained elevated while awaiting additional data.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger growth alongside persistent inflation supports maintaining or increasing restriction rather than resuming an easing cycle.

sources.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as midterm elections loom
sources.evidence_text: The Fed left rates unchanged and indicated that policymakers were waiting for more economic data before deciding on the next policy move.
sources.why_it_matters: A data-dependent pause leaves the policy path open, although the elevated inflation backdrop limits immediate easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3.75%–4.00%, cited elevated inflation, and said additional information would guide the appropriate policy stance.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold amid elevated inflation and reduced forward guidance suggests less urgency to continue easing.

sources.title: FOMC Press Conference
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The chair emphasized persistent inflation concerns, stronger economic growth, and the absence of a preset path for future rates.
sources.why_it_matters: The communication preserves optionality for a prolonged hold or renewed tightening rather than signaling imminent cuts.

sources.title: US Fed Meeting Highlights: Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged
sources.evidence_text: The report described an unchanged policy rate, persistent inflation concerns, and no clear signal that the committee would cut or hike at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A data-dependent stance without easing guidance points to a continued restrictive regime.

sources.title: FOMC press conference, October 28, 2026
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The chair stressed the need to restore price stability while providing limited forward guidance after the decision to hold rates unchanged.
sources.why_it_matters: Emphasis on inflation control and uncertainty about the next move points away from an active cutting cycle.

sources.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady despite inflation concerns
sources.evidence_text: September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, while September payroll growth was only 29,000 and unemployment increased to 4.2%.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation materially above target argues against cuts, although weak hiring creates a competing reason to ease.

sources.title: Meeting calendars and information
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve calendar records the October 27–28, 2026 FOMC meeting and indicates that meeting minutes are released three weeks after the policy decision.
sources.why_it_matters: The calendar confirms the policy-event timing but does not yet provide evidence that the reaction function is shifting toward easing or tightening.

sources.title: TREASURIES-Short-term Treasury yields fall as Fed prompts rethink of rate-hike wagers
sources.evidence_text: The Fed held rates steady while markets still priced roughly a 78% probability of a December hike, and the two-year Treasury yield was about 4.68%.
sources.why_it_matters: A high probability of a near-term hike and an elevated two-year yield indicate markets expect policy to move away from easing.

sources.title: 10-year Treasury yield hovers below 5% after strong GDP report, rising inflation data
sources.evidence_text: The two-year Treasury yield traded near 4.635%, while CME FedWatch showed an 83% probability of a quarter-point December hike after the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4%.
sources.why_it_matters: Short-maturity yields and futures pricing are signaling fewer cuts and a meaningful risk of additional tightening.

sources.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity
sources.evidence_text: The daily two-year Treasury constant-maturity yield was 4.70% on October 27, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The two-year yield is closely tied to expected near-term Fed policy, and its level is inconsistent with markets pricing an imminent return to easing.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Outlook - Singapore
sources.evidence_text: The report said the FOMC held rates by a 10–2 vote and futures priced an approximately 85% probability of a 25-basis-point December hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A divided hold combined with high hike odds suggests the reaction function is biased toward further tightening rather than additional cuts.

sources.title: US Federal Reserve Keeps Rates Unchanged Despite Elevated Inflation
sources.evidence_text: The Fed kept its policy rate unchanged, described inflation as elevated, and indicated that it was waiting for more information before deciding its next step.
sources.why_it_matters: Holding rates amid elevated inflation preserves restrictive policy and leaves the next move more likely to be a hike than a cut.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady despite concerns over inflation
sources.evidence_text: The post-meeting communication said inflation remains elevated and that more information is needed before determining the appropriate policy stance.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent inflation and a data-dependent posture reduce the likelihood of immediate cuts and preserve the option of further tightening.

sources.title: Perspective: Morning Commentary for October 29
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch pricing indicated roughly an 83% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the December FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing for a hike at the next meeting indicates expectations are drifting away from easing and toward renewed tightening.

sources.title: Fed Policy Monitor: Supporting a timelier return to target
sources.evidence_text: The report said OIS markets assigned less than a 10% probability to an immediate follow-on hike after the October decision.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-term OIS pricing supports a pause rather than immediate tightening, although it does not establish an easing path.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady as it awaits accumulation of more information
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC held rates in a 3.75% to 4.00% range, described inflation as elevated, and upgraded its assessment of economic activity.
sources.why_it_matters: Elevated inflation alongside stronger activity supports maintaining restrictive policy and weighs against near-term easing.

sources.title: Treasury yields tick higher after Fed interest rate decision
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield fell more than 3 basis points to 4.704%, while futures priced an 85.7% probability of a 25-basis-point December rate hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A high probability of a near-term hike and an elevated policy-sensitive 2-year yield indicate markets expect tighter policy rather than further easing.

sources.title: Fed keeps interest rates unchanged, but two officials dissent
sources.evidence_text: Markets expected the Fed to hold rates in October, but the probability of a December hike rose to about 85% from 78% the previous day.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising odds of a December hike imply a meaningful shift away from an easing regime in the market-implied reaction function.

sources.title: Analysis-Fed highlights economic strength but muddies outlook
sources.evidence_text: Following the Fed decision, the yield curve steepened and longer-maturity Treasury yields rose as investors assessed the possibility of further tightening and higher term premiums.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher yields and concern about additional tightening suggest financial conditions are not moving toward an easier policy stance.
